run.preReadNotes:
Mode: filter mode (default).

Step 1, plain statement. Six numbered bins (1 to 6) each hold a whole-number count, never negative. Each bin has a fixed capacity, an upper threshold and a lower threshold (lower < upper <= capacity), and a two-value flag (call it OFF/ON; the document calls them QUIET/SINK-ACTIVE), all OFF at start. Running loss counter starts at 0. Five rounds, each: (1) add a fixed per-round, per-bin amount from a table, no cap; (2) sweep bins 1 to 6 in order: anything over capacity moves to the next higher bin (bin 6's overflow is lost), bin set to capacity, cascades within the same sweep; (3) flag flip with hysteresis: OFF becomes ON at count >= upper, ON becomes OFF at count <= lower, else unchanged, at most one change per round; (4) simultaneously compute floor(count/4) for OFF bins (lost) and floor(count/2) for ON bins (moved to the next lower bin; bin 1's goes to loss); capacity not enforced; (5) if total > 38, every bin becomes floor(half), removed amount to loss. Conservation: start + all additions = end + loss. The material contains no instructions aimed at me beyond the job itself. The plain statement fully specifies the procedure, so in filter mode the run could stop here; pictures are run below only to note where the plant wording could mislead a reader.

Steps 2 to 4, pictures (the document's own embedded comparison, tested first and not counted against the three; no further pictures added, since the restatement already settles the job).
Picture A: plant vascular system. Mapping: segments = bins; sap = count; xylem push = upward overflow cascade; phloem return = downward transfer from ON bins; respiration/transpiration = loss counter; leaf-drop = global halving. Question it makes easier to ask: which direction does each flow go? Break points: real xylem moves water up driven by transpiration, not by capacity overflow; real phloem flows from source to sink, but here SINK-ACTIVE segments are the ones sending sap away (toward the root), the reverse of what the word "sink" suggests; real plants have no hard halving rule at a total of 38; "QUIET respires a quarter" has no botanical basis. The word "sink" sneaks in an expectation (sinks receive) that contradicts the stated rule (SINK-ACTIVE segments give half away). Grading: the picture works only as labels; where it carries a mechanism (sink receives), it contradicts the document. Misleading on the sink direction; otherwise adds nothing.

Steps 5 to 7. What survives in plain words: bins with the ON flag send half their contents to the lower neighbour; bins with the OFF flag lose a quarter; overflow moves upward. Adds nothing: 0 of 1. Misleading: 1. Not run: 0. Keep exploring: empty. Hold: empty. Discard: plant vascular picture, break point: "SINK-ACTIVE" segments are donors, not receivers, contradicting the botanical meaning of sink; follow the document's literal rule.
run.rulesInOwnWords:
1. Start: sap [3,6,6,2,2,1], all QUIET, loss 0. Capacities [10,8,12,6,9,7], upper marks [7,6,9,5,7,5], lower marks [3,2,4,2,3,2].
2. Each cycle, step 1: add that cycle's uptake row to each segment, no cap.
3. Step 2: go segment 1 to 6 in order; if sap > capacity, move the excess into the next segment up (segment 6's excess goes to loss) and set sap to capacity. Cascades within the same pass.
4. Step 3: using post-step-2 sap: QUIET with sap >= upper mark becomes SINK-ACTIVE; SINK-ACTIVE with sap <= lower mark becomes QUIET; otherwise unchanged. At most one change per segment per cycle; log each.
5. Step 4: compute all amounts first from current sap: QUIET = floor(sap/4), SINK-ACTIVE = floor(sap/2). Then apply at once: every segment loses its amount; QUIET amounts go to loss; SINK-ACTIVE amounts go to segment n-1 (segment 1's goes to loss). No cap enforced.
6. Step 5: if total sap > 38 (strictly), every segment becomes floor(sap/2), removed amount goes to loss, log the cycle. Exactly 38 does nothing.
7. After cycle 5 step 5, report.
